message.content: {"A0100":"Initially, A0100 accelerated northward in a sustained descent, closing the southbound B pair and preserving a direct firing line. Around step 47 it expended a missile and immediately entered a hard, sustained right turn toward the northeast while the missile continued north; this most plausibly was a post-launch crank to retain pressure but create lateral separation from the head-on exchange and newly airborne B missiles. Late altitude-hold commands began easing the descent, suggesting an effort to preserve maneuvering margin during the offset.","A0200":"A0200 accelerated and descended almost directly north throughout the approach, maintaining rapid closure with the B formation. Around step 50 it expended a missile but, unlike A0100, made no substantial post-launch offset and continued pressing north while its weapon advanced; this most plausibly reflects continued attack commitment intended to sustain favorable geometry and pressure. Even after both B aircraft launched southbound missiles, its only heading changes remained small rather than developing into a defensive break.","B0100":"B0100 maintained a fast southbound descent toward Team A, steadily preserving the head-on attack geometry. After both A aircraft had launched, it expended a missile around step 52 and continued almost straight south rather than turning away; this suggests an offensive commitment intended to keep closure and maintain pressure while its missile advanced. The absence of a meaningful lateral response to the northbound A missiles makes immediate disengagement or missile avoidance less consistent with its observed behavior.","B0200":"B0200 continuously accelerated southward in a descending approach, holding a nearly direct line toward Team A. Around step 47 it expended a missile during the opening exchange with A0100, then continued south without a significant defensive turn; this most plausibly served to preserve attack geometry and maintain pressure while the missile traveled ahead. Its continued commitment despite the simultaneous opposing launch indicates that reducing exposure was secondary to sustaining the engagement during this window."}

{"A0100":"A0100 was already in a hard right, descending break at the window’s start, turning from north toward east while its previously launched missile continued north and Team B’s missiles advanced from that direction. It then stopped tightening the turn and settled into fast, nearly level eastbound flight, most plausibly converting a post-launch defensive maneuver into lateral disengagement that reduced head-on exposure, opened separation from the opposing formation and inbound missile paths, and preserved energy.","A0200":"A0200 initially continued a fast northbound descent toward Team B while its own missile flew ahead, suggesting it was sustaining attack pressure rather than immediately following A0100’s lateral break. Late in the window it began a hard right turn toward the east while continuing down; with both Team B missiles now much closer from the north, this most plausibly marks a delayed defensive break intended to leave the head-on corridor and create lateral separation after the missile exchange.","B0100":"B0100 continued almost straight south throughout, descending and accelerating behind its already outbound missile while maintaining closure with Team A’s initially northbound tracks. Even after A0100 displaced east and the northbound Team A missiles drew substantially closer, B0100 showed no meaningful lateral defense; the behavior therefore most plausibly reflects continued commitment to the attack axis, preserving pressure on the opposing pair and carrying the engagement forward rather than disengaging.","B0200":"B0200 maintained a steady southbound descent and gained speed behind its previously launched missile, remaining particularly well aligned with A0200 while the formations closed. When A0200 eventually began turning east and the Team A missiles approached from the south, B0200 still did not break laterally, suggesting its primary intention remained to press the central attack corridor and sustain closure rather than react defensively or immediately follow the opponent’s lateral maneuver."}

{"A0100":"A0100 maintained a nearly level eastbound offset and steadily accelerated rather than turning back toward the southbound opponents. With its previously launched missile advancing north toward Team B, this perpendicular extension most plausibly preserved post-launch pressure while reducing exposure to the two opposing missiles; when the A missile disappeared as B0200 became inactive, A0100 continued east, consistent with energy preservation and repositioning rather than immediate recommitment.","A0200":"A0200 continued an already-established hard right, descending turn, shifting from northeast toward southeast while accelerating; around mid-window it moderated the turn but sustained the dive and lateral escape. The two Team B missiles remained north of it and progressed southeastward, making this most consistent with dragging or beaming those threats while its own earlier-launched missile continued north. B0200’s loss did not end the maneuver because B0100 and both B missiles remained active.","B0100":"B0100 initially pressed almost straight south in a steep descent, closing on A0200 while its previously launched missile also advanced southeast. After A0200 displaced east and B0200 became inactive, B0100 made a pronounced left turn toward the southeast and continued descending, most plausibly converting the head-on approach into a trailing pursuit of A0200 and maintaining pressure behind the outbound missile. The decreasing separation and increasingly matched direction support pursuit more strongly than disengagement.","B0200":"B0200 began southbound and descending, then progressively rolled into a hard left break that added substantial eastward displacement while continuing downward. Two Team A missiles were approaching northward from directly ahead and closed to its immediate vicinity, so the maneuver most plausibly attempted to spoil their geometry through a lateral defensive turn while retaining speed. B0200 became inactive as both A missiles were removed; the timing is consistent with an unsuccessful defense but does not establish a specific hit."}

{"A0100":"A0100 initially maintained a fast, level eastbound extension without firing or reacting sharply to missiles passing well to its north. From about 48.6 seconds it entered a sustained hard left turn and later descended, curving north and reducing separation from B0100; this most plausibly began a reversal to regain attack geometry against the lone active opponent and potentially relieve A0200, rather than missile evasion, because the recorded missiles were not converging on A0100.","A0200":"A0200 spent the window in a descending, heavily banked east-to-northeast arc, repeatedly adjusting its turn rather than settling into an attack run. This most plausibly attempted to drag and laterally displace B01001, whose near-altitude southeastward path remained behind and north while closing, and to deny pursuit geometry to B0100; by the end A0200 had extended northeast, but neither threat had been decisively separated.","B0100":"B0100 descended on a southeast course toward A0200, then progressively turned east and reduced its sink as the relative bearing shifted, remaining in pursuit behind the Team A aircraft. With no missiles remaining and its already-airborne B01001 following geometry consistent with A0200, this most plausibly maintained pressure and supported the missile engagement rather than disengaging; separation narrowed only modestly as A0200 dragged northeast.","B0200":"B0200 remained inactive with no valid flight state throughout the window, so no tactical intention can be inferred."}

{"A0100":"A0100 descended through a sustained left turn toward B0100, closing from above and expending its final missile once favorable westward attack geometry had developed. It continued the descending turn briefly, then reversed right to avoid remaining committed through the merge and reposition after firing; the missile subsequently converged with B0100, and both were removed together, consistent with the attack defeating B0100 although no hit attribution is recorded.","A0200":"A0200 maintained high speed while arcing from northeast toward north and gradually descending, extending away from B0100 rather than turning back to engage. This most plausibly served as a defensive drag against B0100’s missile, which followed the same northeast corridor behind it throughout the window without clearly closing; A0200 retained its missile and continued the extension even after B0100 became inactive.","B0100":"With its ammunition already exhausted and a missile continuing northeast behind A0200, B0100 initially pursued eastward and progressively turned northeast, plausibly maintaining pressure while its missile engagement developed. After A0100 launched from higher altitude, B0100 transitioned into a steep climbing turn as that missile descended and converged from the northeast, consistent with an attempt to spoil the intercept vertically; B0100 became inactive when the missile was removed, though the record does not independently confirm a hit.","B0200":"B0200 remained inactive with no valid flight state throughout the window, so no tactical intention can be inferred."}
